knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE)

# 1. What this workbook does

This workbook runs the same integration as the Integration tab of the MultiScholaR app, step by step, by calling
the functions the app calls. It reads the tables each omic's workflow saved at its Summary step, matches the
samples across omics, trains a MOFA2 model, shows and saves the results, writes the analysis record and report,
and repeats the analysis from its record to show that it gives the same model.

Every setting comes from the module's settings tables (sections 5 and 6), never from numbers typed here. To change
a setting, put its name and new value in `model_overrides` or `results_overrides`.

**What has been checked against the reference workbook.** The module reproduces the reference workbook's MOFA2
configuration exactly on synthetic data. This shows that the module calls MOFA2 as that workbook did when given the
same settings; it is not a validation of any biological result, and it was not shown on the reference workbook's own
data, which were not available.

**Limitations.** Read these before drawing conclusions from a model.

- At about 20 samples, small or weak signals are not found: in the project's simulations, a factor present only in
  the smaller data sets with a modest signal in each feature was not recovered by any setting. MOFA2's own guidance
  is that factor models need more than about 15 samples. Treat the factors as descriptive.
- Missing values are left out of the model, which treats them as missing at random. Values missing because they
  were below the detection limit are not modelled as such, and MOFA2 fills them with means only to choose its
  starting point.
- The runs of one biological sample are averaged over the values that were observed. When low values are missing
  because they were too low to measure, this average is biased upward for low-abundance features.
- One group of samples (MOFA2's multi-group mode is not used), Gaussian models only, no imputation, and one input
  per omic.
- The agreement with the reference workbook was shown on synthetic data only.
- Pathway and network enrichment depends on external services (STRING, KEGG, Reactome) and their current releases.

# 2. Project folders

The workbook is copied into `<project>/scripts/integration/` when a project is set up. Leave `project_dir` empty
to use that project, or give the project's folder.

```{r folders}
library(MultiScholaR)

project_dir <- if (nzchar(params$project_dir)) params$project_dir else file.path(getwd(), "..", "..")
project_dir <- normalizePath(project_dir, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
results_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "results", "integration")
paths <- list(
    base_dir = project_dir,
    integration_dir = file.path(project_dir, "integration"),
    source_dir = file.path(project_dir, "scripts", "integration"),
    results_dir = results_dir,
    multiomic_inputs_dir = file.path(results_dir, "multiomic_inputs"),
    mofa_tables_dir = file.path(results_dir, "mofa", "tables"),
    mofa_plots_dir = file.path(results_dir, "mofa", "plots"),
    study_report_dir = file.path(project_dir, "results_summary", "integration", "Study_report")
)
dir.create(paths$source_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
project_dir
```

# 3. Find and import the omics' tables

Each omic's Summary step writes its table to `<project>/integration/<omic>/`. The list below shows what was
found; an omic that cannot be used says why.

```{r scan}
scan <- MultiScholaR:::integrationScanProject(paths$integration_dir)
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationScanDisplay(scan))
knitr::kable(scan$views)
```

The data sets of every usable omic are imported into a new store for this analysis.

```{r import}
request <- MultiScholaR:::integrationImportRequest(scan, MultiScholaR:::integrationScanReadyViews(scan)$view)
store_root <- tempfile("integration-store-", tmpdir = paths$source_dir)
manager <- MultiScholaR:::newIntegrationStateOwner(store_root)
MultiScholaR:::importIntegrationInputs(manager, request$dirs)
views <- request$views
views
```

# 4. Match the samples across omics

Samples are matched by the biological sample each omic saved, never by their order. If the omics name one
biological sample differently, edit the table written below (`integration_sample_match_template.tsv`): fill in
`biological_sample` and give the edited file's path as `sample_match_file`.

```{r match}
object <- MultiScholaR:::integrationImportedObject(manager, MultiScholaR:::INTEGRATION_PREVIEW_FIELDS)
match_table <- if (nzchar(params$sample_match_file)) {
    MultiScholaR:::integrationReadSampleMatch(params$sample_match_file)
}
preview <- MultiScholaR:::integrationAlignmentPreview(object, views, match_table, manager = manager)
writeLines(MultiScholaR:::integrationAlignmentFacts(preview))
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationAlignmentViewTable(preview))
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationAlignmentSampleTable(preview))
```

Confirming the match saves the design (and the match, if one was given) for the record.

```{r confirm}
dir.create(paths$multiomic_inputs_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
template <- MultiScholaR:::integrationSampleMatchTemplate(object, preview$parameters$sample_match_table)
utils::write.table(template, file.path(paths$multiomic_inputs_dir, "integration_sample_match_template.tsv"),
    sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
confirmed <- list(
    samples = preview$aligned$samples,
    view_summary = preview$aligned$view_summary,
    parameters = preview$parameters,
    manifests = MultiScholaR:::integrationStateManifests(object),
    file = MultiScholaR:::integrationSaveDesign(preview$aligned$samples, paths$multiomic_inputs_dir),
    confirmed_at = Sys.time()
)
if (!is.null(preview$parameters$sample_match_table)) {
    confirmed$sample_match_file <- MultiScholaR:::integrationSaveSampleMatch(
        preview$parameters$sample_match_table, paths$multiomic_inputs_dir)
}
```

# 5. Train the model

The model's settings and their defaults, with the decision behind each:

```{r model-settings}
model_spec <- MultiScholaR:::integrationMofaParameterSpec()
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationMofaParameterTable())
```

To change a setting, name it here, for example `list(num_factors = 8L)`. How samples are matched (technical
replicates, internal standards, missing samples) is fixed by the confirmed match above, as in the app.

```{r model-train}
model_overrides <- list()
stopifnot(all(names(model_overrides) %in% names(model_spec)))
settings <- lapply(model_spec, `[[`, "default")
settings[names(model_overrides)] <- model_overrides
settings <- settings[setdiff(names(settings), MultiScholaR:::INTEGRATION_GUI_MATCHING_PARAMETERS)]
# Without a feature selection there is no number of features to keep and no observed share.
if (identical(settings$feature_selection, "none")) {
    settings$features_per_view <- NA_integer_
    settings$min_observed_fraction <- NA_real_
}
model_parameters <- MultiScholaR:::integrationModelParameters(confirmed$parameters, settings)
run <- MultiScholaR:::runIntegrationModel(manager, model_parameters,
    confirmation = MultiScholaR:::integrationConfirmationRecord(confirmed))
run_parameters <- manager$.context$snapshot$exports$integration_mofa_model$parameters
model_summary <- MultiScholaR:::integrationModelSummary(run$value, run_parameters)
writeLines(c(model_summary$convergence, model_summary$factors, model_summary$samples, model_summary$saved))
knitr::kable(model_summary$variance)
```

# 6. Results

The results' settings and their defaults:

```{r results-settings}
results_spec <- MultiScholaR:::integrationResultsParameterSpec()
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationResultsParameterTable())
```

```{r results}
results_overrides <- list()
stopifnot(all(names(results_overrides) %in% names(results_spec)))
results_parameters <- lapply(results_spec, `[[`, "default")
results_parameters[names(results_overrides)] <- results_overrides
results <- MultiScholaR:::integrationResults(run$value, MultiScholaR:::integrationImportedObject(manager),
    results_parameters, manager = manager, model_parameters = run_parameters)
writeLines(c(vapply(results$advisories, function(advisory) advisory$sentence, character(1)), results$notes))
```

How much of each data set's variation each factor explains (of the features given to the model), and how stable
each factor is across the training seeds:

```{r results-variance, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotVariance(results))
print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotVarianceTotal(results))
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationResultsVarianceTable(results))
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationResultsStabilityTable(results))
```

The factors against the groups. Read the statement under the figure before reading the table.

```{r results-groups, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotFactorsByGroup(results))
writeLines(MultiScholaR:::integrationClaimLimitText(results))
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationResultsAssociationTable(results))
```

The features with the largest weights, per data set, for the first factor shown (every factor is saved in
section 8), and how the factors correlate with each other:

```{r results-weights, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
for (view in results$views) {
    print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotWeights(results, results$shown[[1L]], view))
}
print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotFactorCorrelation(results))
knitr::kable(MultiScholaR:::integrationResultsCorrelationTable(results))
```

# 7. Further figures

The factors against each other, and the values of the top-weighted features against the first factor shown.
UMAP and t-SNE maps are drawn only when chosen in `results_overrides` (`umap = TRUE`, `tsne = TRUE`).

```{r outputs, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotFactorPairs(results))
for (view in results$views) {
    print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotTopFeatureScatter(results, results$shown[[1L]], view))
    print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotTopFeatureHeatmap(results, results$shown[[1L]], view))
}
drawn <- Filter(function(map) is.null(map$refusal), results$maps)
for (map in Filter(function(map) !is.null(map$refusal), results$maps)) writeLines(map$refusal)
if (length(drawn)) {
    writeLines(MultiScholaR:::integrationMapCaution(results, drawn[[1L]]$settings$samples, names(drawn)))
    for (method in names(drawn)) print(MultiScholaR:::integrationPlotFactorMap(results, method))
}
```

# 8. Save the results

Every table and figure is written to `results/integration/mofa/`.

```{r save}
saved <- MultiScholaR:::integrationSaveResults(manager, run$reference, results, paths)
c(saved$tables, saved$figures)
```

# 9. Record and report

The analysis record, the study parameters, the report, the model file and the sample match are written to the
project's study report folder. The methods paragraph below is written from the record.

```{r record}
bundle <- MultiScholaR:::integrationWriteRecordBundle(manager, paths$study_report_dir, format = params$report_format)
basename(bundle$files)
writeLines(bundle$methods)
```

# 10. Repeat the analysis from its record

The store is closed, reopened and the analysis repeated from its record alone; the repeated model is compared
with the saved one.

```{r replay}
MultiScholaR:::closeWorkflowStateOwner(manager)
replay <- MultiScholaR:::replayIntegrationProject(store_root, tempfile("integration-replay-", tmpdir = paths$source_dir))
knitr::kable(replay$comparison$tables)
if (!is.null(replay$outputs_comparison)) knitr::kable(replay$outputs_comparison$tables)
```
